options.label: Generate the macroscopic description and block key

fields.label: Reaction pattern
fields.help: The pattern sets the diagnosis list and the features offered. Graft-versus-host disease opens its own grading.

reference.title: Reaction patterns
reference.intro: Choose the dominant pattern at scanning power; the diagnosis list and the features follow it.

groups.heading: Spongiotic
points: Intercellular oedema in the epidermis, from slight widening of the spaces to vesicles

images.caption: Subacute spongiotic dermatitis: spongiosis and acanthosis with a superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate (H&E).
images.credit: Yao et al., Arthritis Res Ther 2011, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Mild spongiotic dermatitis: widened intercellular spaces in the lower epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Psoriasiform
points: Elongated rete ridges, regular (psoriasis) or irregular (lichen simplex chronicus)

images.caption: Psoriasis: regular psoriasiform hyperplasia (EH) with confluent parakeratosis and neutrophils in the scale (arrow) (H&E).
images.credit: Giang et al., Front Immunol 2018, via Wikimedia Commons, panel A (cropped)

images.caption: Lichen simplex chronicus: irregular psoriasiform hyperplasia with hyperkeratosis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Interface (vacuolar)
points: Vacuoles and apoptotic keratinocytes along the basal layer with a sparse infiltrate

images.caption: Vacuolar interface dermatitis: vacuolar alteration of the basal layer (arrows) with lymphocytes at the junction between the epidermis (star) and the dermis (circle) (H&E).
images.credit: Heldt Manica and Cohen, Cureus 2017, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Confluent epidermal necrosis lifting off the dermis, as in erythema multiforme, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Interface (lichenoid)
points: A band of lymphocytes in the papillary dermis that obscures the junction

images.caption: Lichen planus: a band of lymphocytes along the junction with loss of basal cells (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: A Civatte body (arrow): an apoptotic keratinocyte at the junction in interface dermatitis (H&E).
images.credit: Kaira et al., Ann Pathol Lab Med 2019, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Perivascular
points: Lymphocytes around superficial, or superficial and deep, vessels with little epidermal change

images.caption: Erythema annulare centrifugum: a tight superficial perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with papillary dermal oedema and focal spongiosis (H&E).
images.credit: Mandel et al., J Med Case Rep 2015, via Wikimedia Commons, panel a (cropped)

images.caption: A wedge-shaped superficial and deep perivascular infiltrate of lymphocytes and eosinophils, as after an insect bite (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Urticaria: dermal oedema (solid arrow) and a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate with eosinophils (dashed arrow), without vasculitis (H&E).
images.credit: Giang et al., Front Immunol 2018, via Wikimedia Commons, panel B (cropped)

groups.heading: Vasculitis
points: Inflammatory cells in vessel walls with fibrinoid necrosis; leukocytoclasia and red cells in small-vessel disease

images.caption: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis: neutrophils, nuclear dust and fibrin around small dermal vessels (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis at high power: fibrinoid change of a small vessel wall with neutrophils and nuclear dust (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Vesiculobullous
points: The level of the split and the cells in the blister; direct immunofluorescence classifies the autoimmune diseases

images.caption: Bullous pemphigoid, confirmed by immunofluorescence: a subepidermal blister with eosinophils in the cavity and the dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Pemphigus vulgaris: a suprabasal acantholytic blister with dermal papillae still lined by basal cells (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Granulomatous
points: Sarcoidal, palisading, interstitial, tuberculoid, suppurative or foreign body

images.caption: Sarcoidosis: discrete epithelioid granulomas with few lymphocytes in the dermis and subcutis (H&E).
images.credit: Jensflorian, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Granuloma annulare: histiocytes in a loose palisade around pale altered collagen in the mid dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Panniculitis
points: Septal or lobular, with or without vasculitis

images.caption: Erythema nodosum: panniculitis (white arrow) with histiocytic infiltrates (yellow arrow) (H&E).
images.credit: Wagle et al., Clin Case Rep 2025, Fig 4, full figure

images.caption: Pancreatic panniculitis: lobular fat necrosis with ghost adipocytes (H&E).
images.credit: Assis and Gomes, Cureus 2025, Fig 4, full figure

groups.heading: Sclerosing
points: Thickened dermal collagen and loss of periadnexal fat, or a homogenised papillary dermis

images.caption: Morphoea: thickened, closely packed collagen bundles through the dermis, with a squared-off outline (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Lichen sclerosus: a pale, homogenised papillary dermis with follicular plugging (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Folliculitis
points: Inflammation of the follicle: neutrophils in acute and infective folliculitis, granulomas around a ruptured follicle; look for yeasts, fungi and Demodex

images.caption: Demodex mites in a dilated follicular infundibulum (H&E).
images.credit: Patho, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Granulomatous folliculitis: multinucleated giant cells around a hair (H&E).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Neutrophilic dermatosis
points: A dense dermal infiltrate of neutrophils without vasculitis, often with papillary dermal oedema: Sweet syndrome and pyoderma gangrenosum, once infection is excluded

images.caption: Sweet syndrome: a dense dermal infiltrate of neutrophils without vasculitis (H&E).
images.credit: Mustafa and Lavizzo, J Med Case Rep 2008, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Sweet syndrome at low power: a dense diffuse infiltrate through the upper dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Ed Uthman, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Graft-versus-host disease
points: Basal vacuolar change with apoptotic keratinocytes in the basal and lower spinous layers, often with adjacent lymphocytes (satellitosis)

images.caption: Acute GVHD: apoptotic keratinocytes in the epidermis with adjacent lymphocytes (satellitosis) (H&E).
images.credit: Mark Ong, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: No significant abnormality
points: Before calling the skin normal, look again for subtle changes: fungal hyphae in the stratum corneum (PASD), sparse dermal neutrophils or eosinophils, amyloid in the dermal papillae and squared-off sclerosis

reference.note: Room for your own photographs of normal skin: no openly licensed image of a normal biopsy taken for a rash was found.

fields.label: Diagnosis
fields.help: The first entry is the pattern itself; the others name a disease.

fields.label: Wording
fields.help: Auto names a disease on its own when the histology is specific, and after the pattern ("..., in keeping with ...") when it needs clinical correlation or immunofluorescence.

fields.label: Vessels
options: Superficial and deep dermal small vessels
Medium-sized vessels at the dermal-subcutaneous junction

map.Medium-vessel vasculitis: Medium-sized vessels at the dermal-subcutaneous junction
map.Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa: Medium-sized vessels at the dermal-subcutaneous junction

reference.title: Vessels involved
reference.intro: The size and depth of the vessels separate small-vessel from medium-vessel disease; deep vessels need a biopsy that reaches the subcutis.

groups.heading: Superficial dermal small vessels
points: Postcapillary venules of the superficial plexus
Leukocytoclastic, IgA and urticarial vasculitis; immunofluorescence on an early lesion identifies IgA vasculitis

images.caption: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis at high power: fibrinoid change of a small vessel wall with neutrophils and nuclear dust (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis: a mixed infiltrate around superficial postcapillary venules with nuclear dust (dashed arrows) (H&E).
images.credit: Giang et al., Front Immunol 2018, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Superficial and deep dermal small vessels
points: Small vessels of both plexuses
Deep involvement raises a systemic vasculitis: ANCA-associated, cryoglobulinaemic or connective tissue disease

images.caption: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis at low power: perivascular infiltrates in the superficial and deep dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Medium-sized vessels at the dermal-subcutaneous junction
points: Muscular arteries at the junction or in the subcutaneous septa
Fibrinoid necrosis and neutrophils in the wall, then thrombosis and fibrosis: cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa

images.caption: Cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa at increasing magnification: ulceration, dermal oedema and fibrinoid necrosis of vessel walls with a mild perivascular infiltrate (H&E).
images.credit: Berardi et al., Medicine (Baltimore) 2023, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Small vessels in the subcutis
points: Calcium in the walls of small subcutaneous vessels with thrombi and fat necrosis: calciphylaxis; a von Kossa stain helps
Vasculitis with lobular panniculitis: erythema induratum (nodular vasculitis)

images.caption: Calciphylaxis at scanning power: calcium deposits in the deep dermis and subcutis, including vessel walls (H&E, x10).
images.credit: Čular et al., Curr Oncol 2026, Fig 3 (cropped)

reference.title: Blister level
reference.intro: Judge the level at the edge of an early blister; an older subepidermal blister can re-epithelialise and look intraepidermal.

groups.heading: Subepidermal
points: The whole epidermis forms the roof
Eosinophils: bullous pemphigoid, pemphigoid gestationis
Neutrophils: dermatitis herpetiformis, linear IgA disease, bullous lupus
Few cells: porphyria cutanea tarda, epidermolysis bullosa acquisita

images.caption: Bullous pemphigoid, confirmed by immunofluorescence: a subepidermal blister with eosinophils in the cavity and the dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Sarahkayb, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Linear IgA disease: a subepidermal blister filled with neutrophils (arrow) (H&E).
images.credit: Saleem and Iftikhar, Cureus 2019, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Pemphigoid gestationis: subepidermal separation with eosinophils (HPS stain).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Suprabasal
points: A cleft just above the basal layer, with acantholytic cells in the cavity
The basal keratinocytes stay on the floor like a row of tombstones
Pemphigus vulgaris; focal suprabasal acantholysis in Darier, Hailey-Hailey and Grover disease

images.caption: Pemphigus vulgaris: rounded acantholytic cells in the cavity above a row of basal keratinocytes (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Pemphigus vulgaris: a suprabasal acantholytic blister with dermal papillae still lined by basal cells (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Intraepidermal
points: A split within the spinous layer
Spongiotic vesicles: eczema, arthropod bites, eosinophilic spongiosis
Ballooning with multinucleated keratinocytes: herpes simplex and varicella-zoster virus

images.caption: Kaposi varicelliform eruption: an intraepidermal blister with acantholysis (top) and infected keratinocytes with multinucleation, chromatin margination and moulding (bottom) (H&E).
images.credit: Goswami et al., Acta Med Litu 2025, Fig 4A-B (cropped)

groups.heading: Subcorneal
points: A split beneath or within the stratum corneum or granular layer
Acantholytic cells: pemphigus foliaceus
Neutrophils: subcorneal pustular dermatosis, IgA pemphigus, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, impetigo

images.caption: Pemphigus foliaceus: a subcorneal split with acantholysis and neutrophils in the upper epidermis (H&E).
images.credit: Ahmad et al., Cureus 2024, Fig 2, full figure

fields.label: Features
options: Neutrophil microabscesses in the dermal papillae

reference.title: Granuloma types
reference.intro: Name the type at scanning power; stains for organisms and polarised light sort the infective and foreign-body types.

groups.heading: Sarcoidal
points: Discrete, rounded epithelioid granulomas with few lymphocytes
Sarcoidosis, once infection and foreign material are excluded

images.caption: Sarcoidosis: discrete epithelioid granulomas with few lymphocytes in the dermis and subcutis (H&E).
images.credit: Jensflorian, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Palisading
points: Histiocytes palisade around altered collagen
Mucin centrally: granuloma annulare; layered bands through the dermis with plasma cells: necrobiosis lipoidica; fibrin: rheumatoid nodule

images.caption: Granuloma annulare: histiocytes in a loose palisade around pale altered collagen in the mid dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Necrobiosis lipoidica: layered granulomatous inflammation through the full dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Interstitial
points: Histiocytes scattered between collagen bundles, without a formed palisade
Interstitial granuloma annulare, interstitial granulomatous dermatitis and drug reaction

images.caption: Granuloma annulare: histiocytes spread between collagen bundles of the mid and deep dermis (H&E).
images.credit: Nephron, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

groups.heading: Tuberculoid
points: Epithelioid granulomas with a cuff of lymphocytes, with or without caseous necrosis
Tuberculosis and tuberculoid leprosy (granulomas along nerves and adnexa); Ziehl-Neelsen and Fite stains

images.caption: Borderline tuberculoid leprosy: a granuloma with lymphocytes disrupting a sweat gland (H&E).
images.credit: SB Lucas, Wellcome Collection, via Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Borderline tuberculoid leprosy: epithelioid granulomas in the dermis with fewer appendages (H&E).
images.credit: Department of Pathology, Calicut Medical College, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Suppurative
points: Neutrophils or a microabscess in the centre of the granuloma
Deep fungal infection (chromoblastomycosis, sporotrichosis), atypical mycobacteria, a ruptured follicle or cyst; PASD, Grocott, Ziehl-Neelsen and culture

images.caption: Chromoblastomycosis: brown sclerotic (Medlar) bodies in a granuloma with giant cells (H&E).
images.credit: Department of Pathology, Calicut Medical College, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Chromoblastomycosis: epidermal hyperplasia over dermal collections of acute inflammatory cells around sclerotic bodies (H&E).
images.credit: Department of Pathology, Calicut Medical College, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Foreign body
points: Foreign-body giant cells, often with the material inside them
Exogenous material (suture, splinters, tattoo pigment; polarise) or endogenous material (keratin and hair from a ruptured follicle or cyst)

images.caption: Hair in the dermis, in longitudinal and cross section, with a foreign-body granulomatous reaction (H&E).
images.credit: Atlas of Medical Foreign Bodies, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Ruptured inclusion cyst: multinucleated giant cells around keratin flakes (H&E).
images.credit: Mikael Häggström, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

reference.title: Panniculitis
reference.intro: Decide whether the septa or the lobules hold most of the inflammation, then look for vasculitis.

groups.heading: Septal
points: Thickened, inflamed septa with the lobules largely spared
Erythema nodosum, with Miescher radial granulomas; also morphoea profunda and necrobiosis lipoidica

images.caption: Erythema nodosum: panniculitis (white arrow) with histiocytic infiltrates (yellow arrow) (H&E).
images.credit: Wagle et al., Clin Case Rep 2025, Fig 4, full figure

images.caption: Erythema nodosum: a Miescher radial granuloma (circled) (H&E).
images.credit: Wagle et al., Clin Case Rep 2025, Fig 3, full figure

groups.heading: Lobular
points: Inflammation within the fat lobules, usually with fat necrosis
Lupus panniculitis (lymphoid follicles, hyaline fat necrosis), pancreatic panniculitis (ghost adipocytes, saponification), erythema induratum (with vasculitis) and infection
Exclude subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma

images.caption: Pancreatic panniculitis: lobular fat necrosis with ghost adipocytes (H&E).
images.credit: Assis and Gomes, Cureus 2025, Fig 4, full figure

groups.heading: Septal and lobular
points: Both compartments inflamed
Lipodermatosclerosis (septal fibrosis, lipomembranous change), late erythema nodosum, infection and trauma

reference.note: Room for your own photographs: no openly licensed image of lipodermatosclerosis or another mixed septal and lobular panniculitis was found.

fields.label: Features
options: Band-like infiltrate beneath the sclerotic zone

fields.label: NIH category
fields.help: The NIH 2014 final categories. Possible GVHD: name the other explanations in the differential.

reference.title: NIH 2014 categories
reference.intro: Final categories for a biopsy taken for GVHD; no single feature is pathognomonic.

groups.heading: Categories
points: Not GVHD: no evidence for GVHD
Possible GVHD: evidence of GVHD but other possible explanations, such as a drug reaction; name them

Likely GVHD: clear evidence of GVHD without a competing cause, or with mitigating factors, or GVHD the most likely diagnosis on limited clinical information; includes the former "consistent with" and "unequivocal" categories

Minimal criterion: apoptosis in the basal or lower spinous layer, the follicular infundibulum or outer root sheath, or the acrosyringium, with or without lichenoid inflammation, vacuolar change and satellitosis
Eosinophils often occur in GVHD and do not by themselves indicate a drug reaction

images.caption: Acute GVHD: apoptotic keratinocytes in the epidermis with adjacent lymphocytes (satellitosis) (H&E).
images.credit: Mark Ong, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Acute GVHD: apoptotic keratinocytes with lymphocyte satellitosis in another field (H&E).
images.credit: Mark Ong, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Chronic GVHD patterns
points: Lichen planus-like: orthohyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis and acanthosis, with or without lichenoid inflammation or vacuolar change of eccrine units
Morphoea-like: thickened homogenised collagen through the reticular dermis, or pandermal sclerosis, with overlying interface change
Lichen sclerosus-like: homogenised papillary dermis with interface change, melanophages and a sparse infiltrate
Fasciitis: thickened fascial septa with adjacent inflammation

reference.note: Room for your own photographs: no openly licensed images of chronic GVHD at a useful resolution were found.

fields.label: Features
default: Apoptotic keratinocytes in the basal layer
options: Apoptotic keratinocytes in the basal layer
Apoptotic keratinocytes in the lower spinous layer
Apoptotic cells in the follicular epithelium

fields.label: Lerner grade
fields.help: Auto reads the grade from the features ticked: I basal vacuolar change, II apoptotic keratinocytes, III subepidermal clefts, IV separation of the epidermis. Printed with Likely GVHD only.

reference.title: Lerner grade (acute GVHD)
reference.intro: Grades the epidermal injury of acute GVHD at its most damaged point; 0 is normal skin, and chronic GVHD is not graded this way.

groups.heading: I
points: Vacuolar change of the basal keratinocytes

images.caption: Grade I: vacuolar change of the basal keratinocytes (skin explant assay, H&E).
images.credit: Ghimire et al., Front Immunol 2017, via Wikimedia Commons, grade I panel (cropped)

groups.heading: II
points: As grade I, with apoptotic (dyskeratotic) keratinocytes

images.caption: Grade II: vacuolar change with dyskeratotic keratinocytes (arrows) (skin explant assay, H&E).
images.credit: Ghimire et al., Front Immunol 2017, via Wikimedia Commons, grade II panel (cropped)

groups.heading: III
points: Subepidermal cleft formation

images.caption: Grade III: subepidermal clefts (arrows) (skin explant assay, H&E).
images.credit: Ghimire et al., Front Immunol 2017, via Wikimedia Commons, grade III panel (cropped)

groups.heading: IV
points: Complete separation of the epidermis from the dermis

images.caption: Grade IV: complete separation of the epidermis from the dermis (arrows) (skin explant assay, H&E).
images.credit: Ghimire et al., Front Immunol 2017, via Wikimedia Commons, grade IV panel (cropped)

reference.note: The photographs come from a human skin explant assay graded on the same scale, not from patient biopsies.

fields.label: Distribution
options: Superficial and deep perivascular and periadnexal

reference.title: Direct immunofluorescence
reference.intro: The deposit, its site and its pattern; the reagents not named print as negative.

groups.heading: Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone
points: Bullous pemphigoid and epidermolysis bullosa acquisita
n-serrated in pemphigoid; u-serrated only in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita

images.caption: n-serrated (left) and u-serrated (right) linear deposits along the basement membrane zone (direct immunofluorescence).
images.credit: Witte et al., Front Med (Lausanne) 2018, Fig 3, full figure

groups.heading: Linear IgA along the basement membrane zone
points: Linear IgA disease, including chronic bullous disease of childhood

images.caption: Linear IgA along the basement membrane (arrow) in linear IgA bullous dermatosis of a child (direct immunofluorescence).
images.credit: Khalid et al., Cureus 2026, Fig 4, full figure

groups.heading: Intercellular IgG and C3 in the epidermis
points: Pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus foliaceus; the level of the split, not the deposit, separates them

images.caption: Pemphigus vulgaris: intercellular IgG through the epidermis, with an early acantholytic vesicle (direct immunofluorescence).
images.credit: Emmanuelm, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

images.caption: Pemphigus foliaceus: intercellular IgG and C3 in the epidermis (direct immunofluorescence).
images.credit: Ahmad et al., Cureus 2024, Fig 3A (cropped)

groups.heading: Granular IgA in the dermal papillae
points: Dermatitis herpetiformis; sample perilesional skin

images.caption: Dermatitis herpetiformis: granular IgA at the tips of the dermal papillae and along the junction (direct immunofluorescence).
images.credit: van Beek et al., Front Immunol 2024, Fig 5A (cropped)

groups.heading: Perivascular IgA and C3 in superficial dermal vessels
points: IgA vasculitis; deposits fade from older lesions, so sample an early one

images.caption: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura): IgA in the walls of small superficial vessels (arrows) (direct immunofluorescence).
images.credit: Emmanuelm, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: Granular IgG, IgM and C3 along the basement membrane zone
points: Lupus erythematosus: the lupus band

images.caption: Systemic lupus erythematosus: a band of IgG along the epidermal basement membrane, with IgG also in keratinocyte nuclei (direct immunofluorescence).
images.credit: Emmanuelm, Wikimedia Commons, full figure

groups.heading: IgM-positive cytoid bodies
points: Clumps of IgM, often with IgA, IgG, C3 and fibrin, on apoptotic keratinocytes in the papillary dermis
Lichen planus and other interface dermatitides

reference.note: Room for your own photographs: no openly licensed image of IgM-positive cytoid bodies was found.
